items.title: Invitation to bid for up to £75,000 to improve community paediatric waiting times
items.summary: GIRFT is inviting NHS-commissioned community paediatric service providers in England to express interest in bidding for up to £75,000 of funding to improve waiting times for community paediatric services.

items.title: Vomiting in infants: when is it reflux, and when should we worry?
items.summary: Dilemmas in paediatrics: GPwER in paediatrics Dr David Capehorn discusses how to assess the vomiting infant, and distinguish normal physiology, overfeeding and milk allergy from the rare scenarios where a child needs urgent referral Note cases discussed in this article are hypothetical and created for educational…

items.title: Infant feeding and mental health support to be rolled out across England by 2028
items.summary: A ‘Healthy Babies’ programme like what used to be provided in Sure Start centres will be rolled out to all local authorities by 2028, the Government has announced.

items.title: Implementing Benedict’s law: guidance from a school nurse
items.summary: Following the launch of new statutory allergy safety guidance this month, all state-maintained schools, academies and free schools are expected to meet a number of requirements relating to staff allergy training and allergy safety policies, among other things.

items.title: Children as young as 13 seen by NHS for bladder damage caused by ketamine
items.summary: Children as young as 13 for bladder problems associated with ketamine use according to doctors who set up an NHS clinic to manage the problem.

items.title: Provisional childhood vaccine coverage in England: July 2026
items.summary: UKHSA's monthly provisional estimates from GP data for MMRV, rotavirus, MenB, the 6-in-1 and the dTaP/IPV booster in July 2026. Supplements the official COVER statistics to give immunisation teams more timely figures; local authority figures vary because cohorts are small.

items.title: Childhood vaccination coverage (COVER) April to June 2026: 12-month coverage slips
items.summary: UKHSA's COVER data for Q1 2026/27: in England 12-month coverage fell to 89.2% for the 6-in-1, 89.5% for PCV1 and 87.6% for rotavirus, while MenB rose to 91.4%. Coverage stays below its 10-year peaks and is lowest in London and deprived areas.

items.title: Pertussis in England: 71 confirmed cases in January to March 2026
items.summary: UKHSA confirmed 71 whooping cough cases in Q1 2026, similar to Q4 2025 (77) and far below Q1 2025 (328), as the 2024 cyclical peak continues to recede. 79% were aged 15 or over; 3 were infants, one under 3 months. Infant under-3-month cases fell from 433 in 2024 to 12 in 2025.

items.title: Jiraffe relaunches children's postural care range after demand
items.summary: THIIS reported that Jiraffe's postural care range for children with cerebral palsy and similar conditions has returned following demand, restoring clinician access to those products.

items.title: Concerns raised as data reveals ‘dramatic and significant’ decline in health visitors and school nurses across England
items.summary: Concerns have been raised by community nursing associations as new data has revealed a ‘dramatic and significant’ decline in the number of health visitors and school nurses across England.

items.title: ‘Alarming’ rise in children attending A&E in mental health crisis
items.summary: A growing number of children and young people ending up in A&E with mental health concerns because of a lack of alternative options is a ‘national crisis’, the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH) has warned.

items.title: Many GPs cannot access key asthma test for children
items.summary: GPs across large parts of the country cannot access a key, NICE-recommended test for diagnosing asthma in children, a charity has warned.

items.title: Weight-loss injections cut obesity rates in children, study finds
items.summary: Two-in-five children living with obesity achieved a body mass index (BMI) below the obesity threshold when taking weight-loss injections, a new study has found.

items.title: MenB behind 92% of meningococcal disease cases in infants
items.summary: Meningitis B (MenB) accounted for 92% of invasive meningococcal disease cases among infants in England in 2025/26 and all cases among children aged one to four, according to new figures from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: UKHSA issues warning as only half of school children had flu vaccine last year
items.summary: Only half of primary school children had a flu vaccine last year, with uptake still below that achieved before the pandemic, officials said.

items.title: Only around half of eligible primary school children had a flu vaccine last year
items.summary: Around two million eligible primary school children went without a flu vaccine last year, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has revealed. New data shows only around half (55.5%) of primary school children – reception to year 6 – had the flu vaccine during the 2025/26 winter season.

items.summary: Journal of Wound Care, Volume 35, Issue 9, Page 760-766, September 2026.…

items.title: Rise in children’s A&E mental health visits prompts call for nurse investment
items.summary: A rise in children and young people (CYP) attending A&E departments with mental health concerns has prompted calls for new and sustained investment in specialist nursing roles.

items.title: Government investigating school nursing provision and challenges
items.summary: The government has commissioned research into how school nursing services are currently being delivered across England.
